This is exploratory guidance only: consult the connected Playbook, explain prerequisites and limitations, and do not edit this checkout or choose a target framework for that application.

      "markdown": "# Model distinct outcomes with a C# union\n\n## Goal\n\nReturn either an archive receipt or a refusal without accepting arbitrary objects. Use a union when the alternatives already exist as unrelated types and callers should handle each case. The museum example keeps a shelf location separate from a refusal reason; both remain recoverable after persistence.\n\n## Older approach\n\n.NET 10 / C# 14 has no union declaration. A small wrapper with typed constructors can constrain assignment while retaining unrelated payload types. Matching its object-valued property needs a defensive fallback because the compiler cannot infer the complete set. This remains a valid choice for an older target or a deliberately custom representation.\n\nIn a console project targeting net10.0 with LangVersion 14.0, use `using System.Text.Json;`, `using System.Text.Json.Serialization;` and the file-scoped namespace `Playbook.Samples`. The following model, converter and context are complete together:\n\n```csharp\npublic sealed record ArchiveReceipt([property: JsonRequired] string ShelfCode);\npublic sealed record ArchiveRefusal([property: JsonRequired] string ReasonCode);\n\n[JsonConverter(typeof(OutcomeConverter))]\npublic readonly struct Outcome\n{\n    public Outcome(ArchiveReceipt receipt) => Value = receipt;\n    public Outcome(ArchiveRefusal refusal) => Value = refusal;\n    public object? Value { get; }\n}\n\npublic static class OutcomeWorkflow\n{\n    public static Outcome Receipt(string shelf) => new(new ArchiveReceipt(shelf));\n    public static Outcome Refusal(string reason) => new(new ArchiveRefusal(reason));\n    public static string Describe(Outcome outcome) => outcome.Value switch\n    {\n        ArchiveReceipt receipt => \"stored:\" + receipt.ShelfCode,\n        ArchiveRefusal refusal => \"refused:\" + refusal.ReasonCode,\n        null => \"unassigned\",\n        _ => throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Unexpected outcome type.\")\n    };\n\n    public static string Serialize(Outcome outcome) => JsonSerializer.Serialize(outcome, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n    public static Outcome Deserialize(string json) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n}\n```\n```csharp\npublic sealed class OutcomeConverter : JsonConverter<Outcome>\n{\n    public override Outcome Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)\n    {\n        if (reader.TokenType == JsonTokenType.Null) { return default; }\n        using JsonDocument document = JsonDocument.ParseValue(ref reader);\n        JsonElement root = document.RootElement;\n        if (root.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) { throw new JsonException(\"Expected an archive outcome object.\"); }\n        bool receipt = root.TryGetProperty(\"ShelfCode\", out _);\n        bool refusal = root.TryGetProperty(\"ReasonCode\", out _);\n        if (receipt == refusal) { throw new JsonException(\"Expected exactly one archive outcome case.\"); }\n        return receipt\n            ? new Outcome(root.Deserialize(OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveReceipt) ?? throw new JsonException())\n            : new Outcome(root.Deserialize(OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveRefusal) ?? throw new JsonException());\n    }\n\n    public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, Outcome value, JsonSerializerOptions options)\n    {\n        switch (value.Value)\n        {\n            case ArchiveReceipt receipt: JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, receipt, OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveReceipt); break;\n            case ArchiveRefusal refusal: JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, refusal, OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveRefusal); break;\n            case null: writer.WriteNullValue(); break;\n            default: throw new JsonException(\"Unexpected outcome type.\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n```csharp\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(Outcome))]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(ArchiveReceipt))]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(ArchiveRefusal))]\ninternal partial class OutcomeJson : JsonSerializerContext;\n```\n\n## Newer approach\n\nTarget net11.0 with LangVersion 15.0. Keep the same imports and namespace. The compiler supplies a struct wrapper, constructors, implicit conversions and union-aware matching. The null arm is intentional: default storage has no active case. The JSON attribute selects between two object-shaped payloads by required root properties. The metadata context supplies serialization contracts without reflection-based fallback.\n\n```csharp\npublic sealed record ArchiveReceipt([property: JsonRequired] string ShelfCode);\npublic sealed record ArchiveRefusal([property: JsonRequired] string ReasonCode);\n\n[JsonUnion(TypeClassifier = typeof(JsonUnionTypeStructuralClassifier))]\npublic union Outcome(ArchiveReceipt, ArchiveRefusal);\n\npublic static class OutcomeWorkflow\n{\n    public static Outcome Receipt(string shelf) => new ArchiveReceipt(shelf);\n    public static Outcome Refusal(string reason) => new ArchiveRefusal(reason);\n    public static string Describe(Outcome outcome) => outcome switch\n    {\n        ArchiveReceipt receipt => \"stored:\" + receipt.ShelfCode,\n        ArchiveRefusal refusal => \"refused:\" + refusal.ReasonCode,\n        null => \"unassigned\"\n    };\n\n    public static string Serialize(Outcome outcome) => JsonSerializer.Serialize(outcome, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n    public static Outcome Deserialize(string json) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n}\n```\n```csharp\n[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(GenerationMode = JsonSourceGenerationMode.Metadata)]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(Outcome))]\ninternal partial class OutcomeJson : JsonSerializerContext;\n```\n\nFor example, `Outcome value = OutcomeWorkflow.Receipt(\"C-24\");` followed by `OutcomeWorkflow.Describe(value)` returns `stored:C-24`. Serializing and deserializing through these helpers retains that result. Use `OutcomeWorkflow.Refusal(\"humidity\")` to get the distinct `refused:humidity` result. See recipe `json.serialize-closed-results` for the classification and persistence tradeoffs.\n\n## Migration\n\n1. Keep each payload's meaning and validation rules. Replace the handwritten wrapper with the union declaration; remove only that wrapper's now-redundant constructors and storage.\n2. Switch on the union itself instead of its Value property. Handle every payload plus null; treat an unassigned result deliberately instead of inventing a successful payload.\n3. Retain the JSON classifier and generated context when persisting these object cases. Test existing payloads before removing the old converter.\n4. Compile consumers with warnings treated as errors. Adding a third case must force review of incomplete switch expressions; don't mask it with a discard arm.\n5. Escape existing type identifiers named `union` or `closed` as `@union` or `@closed` at declaration and affected uses when migrating to C# 15.\n\n## Constraints\n\nThis route needs .NET 11 runtime/reference assemblies and the .NET 11 SDK with C# 15. No preview language flag, extra package, workload, provider, UI framework or rendering mode is used. No supported down-level C# 15 route is claimed. The verification baseline is RC2, not GA verification.\n\nA declared union stores object-backed state; value-type payloads box. It supplies neither record equality nor a domain-specific empty case. `default(Outcome)` has null Value; JSON null maps to that default when no case accepts null. Nullable wrapper absence and empty underlying storage can both match null. Do not rely on a nullability annotation to make default impossible. Union declarations cannot add instance fields, auto-properties, field-like events or public single-parameter constructors. Custom union implementations must obey the compiler's soundness and access rules; this recipe uses the generated representation.\n\nExhaustiveness diagnoses omitted known cases; it does not validate payload properties or prove persisted data is trustworthy. Use a closed hierarchy when the alternatives need common inherited members (`csharp.closed-hierarchies`).\n\n## Evidence\n\nThe original .NET 10/C# 14 and .NET 11 RC2/C# 15 projects compile and execute the same case/payload, null/default and JSON ambiguity checks. The .NET 11 consumer probe omits a union case and requires CS8509, promoted to an error. Evidence records retain exact SDKs, dependencies, inputs and actual output. No mocks, Native AOT publishing, GA execution or UI/client matrix is represented as proof. Portable execution needs no targeted Human proof.\n"
    }
  }
}

      "markdown": "# Preserve a union's distinct cases through JSON\n\n## Goal\n\nPersist unrelated result types without losing which outcome occurred. Use this when JSON must retain both case identity and payload, and when its shape can select a case unambiguously. The archive receipt has a required ShelfCode; a refusal has a required ReasonCode. Neither is encoded as an arbitrary object with guessed runtime type.\n\n## Older approach\n\nIn .NET 10, an explicit converter can read the object, choose exactly one case and delegate payload handling to source-generated contracts. This offers direct control of the wire contract and remains valid when selection depends on business rules. It also means the application owns that selection code.\n\nFor a net10.0 / C# 14 console project, add `using System.Text.Json;`, `using System.Text.Json.Serialization;` and namespace `Playbook.Samples`. These three canonical blocks form the complete model and serialization setup:\n\n```csharp\npublic sealed record ArchiveReceipt([property: JsonRequired] string ShelfCode);\npublic sealed record ArchiveRefusal([property: JsonRequired] string ReasonCode);\n\n[JsonConverter(typeof(OutcomeConverter))]\npublic readonly struct Outcome\n{\n    public Outcome(ArchiveReceipt receipt) => Value = receipt;\n    public Outcome(ArchiveRefusal refusal) => Value = refusal;\n    public object? Value { get; }\n}\n\npublic static class OutcomeWorkflow\n{\n    public static Outcome Receipt(string shelf) => new(new ArchiveReceipt(shelf));\n    public static Outcome Refusal(string reason) => new(new ArchiveRefusal(reason));\n    public static string Describe(Outcome outcome) => outcome.Value switch\n    {\n        ArchiveReceipt receipt => \"stored:\" + receipt.ShelfCode,\n        ArchiveRefusal refusal => \"refused:\" + refusal.ReasonCode,\n        null => \"unassigned\",\n        _ => throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Unexpected outcome type.\")\n    };\n\n    public static string Serialize(Outcome outcome) => JsonSerializer.Serialize(outcome, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n    public static Outcome Deserialize(string json) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n}\n```\n```csharp\npublic sealed class OutcomeConverter : JsonConverter<Outcome>\n{\n    public override Outcome Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)\n    {\n        if (reader.TokenType == JsonTokenType.Null) { return default; }\n        using JsonDocument document = JsonDocument.ParseValue(ref reader);\n        JsonElement root = document.RootElement;\n        if (root.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) { throw new JsonException(\"Expected an archive outcome object.\"); }\n        bool receipt = root.TryGetProperty(\"ShelfCode\", out _);\n        bool refusal = root.TryGetProperty(\"ReasonCode\", out _);\n        if (receipt == refusal) { throw new JsonException(\"Expected exactly one archive outcome case.\"); }\n        return receipt\n            ? new Outcome(root.Deserialize(OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveReceipt) ?? throw new JsonException())\n            : new Outcome(root.Deserialize(OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveRefusal) ?? throw new JsonException());\n    }\n\n    public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, Outcome value, JsonSerializerOptions options)\n    {\n        switch (value.Value)\n        {\n            case ArchiveReceipt receipt: JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, receipt, OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveReceipt); break;\n            case ArchiveRefusal refusal: JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, refusal, OutcomeJson.Default.ArchiveRefusal); break;\n            case null: writer.WriteNullValue(); break;\n            default: throw new JsonException(\"Unexpected outcome type.\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n```csharp\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(Outcome))]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(ArchiveReceipt))]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(ArchiveRefusal))]\ninternal partial class OutcomeJson : JsonSerializerContext;\n```\n\n## Newer approach\n\n.NET 11's serializer writes the active union payload directly, without a case wrapper or discriminator. Token kinds distinguish primitive-shaped cases, but both of our cases are objects. JsonUnionTypeStructuralClassifier narrows candidates using root property names and required-property metadata. JsonRequired makes the distinction explicit. The generated metadata context registers the union and supplies its case contracts.\n\nIn net11.0 with LangVersion 15.0, use the same imports and namespace:\n\n```csharp\npublic sealed record ArchiveReceipt([property: JsonRequired] string ShelfCode);\npublic sealed record ArchiveRefusal([property: JsonRequired] string ReasonCode);\n\n[JsonUnion(TypeClassifier = typeof(JsonUnionTypeStructuralClassifier))]\npublic union Outcome(ArchiveReceipt, ArchiveRefusal);\n\npublic static class OutcomeWorkflow\n{\n    public static Outcome Receipt(string shelf) => new ArchiveReceipt(shelf);\n    public static Outcome Refusal(string reason) => new ArchiveRefusal(reason);\n    public static string Describe(Outcome outcome) => outcome switch\n    {\n        ArchiveReceipt receipt => \"stored:\" + receipt.ShelfCode,\n        ArchiveRefusal refusal => \"refused:\" + refusal.ReasonCode,\n        null => \"unassigned\"\n    };\n\n    public static string Serialize(Outcome outcome) => JsonSerializer.Serialize(outcome, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n    public static Outcome Deserialize(string json) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, OutcomeJson.Default.Outcome);\n}\n```\n```csharp\n[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(GenerationMode = JsonSourceGenerationMode.Metadata)]\n[JsonSerializable(typeof(Outcome))]\ninternal partial class OutcomeJson : JsonSerializerContext;\n```\n\nSerializing `OutcomeWorkflow.Receipt(\"C-24\")` produces `{\"ShelfCode\":\"C-24\"}`; the refusal produces `{\"ReasonCode\":\"humidity\"}`. Inventory persisted shapes and choose a stable way to select exactly one case. Do not assume two object cases are distinguished automatically by their CLR names.\n2. Declare the union, annotate its structural classifier and mark the identifying properties required. Supply the metadata context and pass its JsonTypeInfo to both serialization calls.\n3. Round-trip each case and check both its identity and payload. Test unmatched and ambiguous inputs, not only successful writes.\n4. Decide how JSON null behaves. In this union no case accepts null, so it becomes default storage and serializes back to null; the matching helper returns `unassigned`.\n5. Remove the old converter only after compatibility checks. Zero or multiple candidates throw JsonException. It does not support nested unions, polymorphic cases, multiple non-object cases sharing one JSON token kind, or ReferenceHandler.Preserve.
